bugs: QueueStatementJobs is #[Tries(3)] (app/Jobs/QueueStatementJobs.php:14) and not idempotent. If it fails partway through the fan-out and retries, it re-adds every chunk, so accounts get duplicate statements and emails and failures can be double-counted
No pruning is scheduled for job_batches or failed_jobs (routes/console.php unchanged), so the queue tables grow forever. That breaks a stated requirement

total_accounts is counted in the request, but the active accounts are re-queried later inside the fan-out job. If accounts change between the two (my probe deleted one), the run reports 3 total and 0 failed while only 2 were attempted
antipatterns: app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:41 catches every Throwable and counts it as a failure. A transient SMTP or S3 error is never retried, and failed_jobs loses the record (it only goes to report())
app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:18 #[Tries(1)] means one transient failure is a permanent failure for that month's statement
app/Actions/FinalizeStatementRun.php:13 is a batch callback object that holds runId state, but it sits in App\Actions next to the request-side action
Failures are counted manually with increment, which duplicates what the batch already tracks
strengths: Statement jobs run on a configurable 'statements' queue with lazyById chunked fan-out into the batch; the fan-out job is part of the batch, so the batch cannot finish early
Finalize is atomic: a conditional UPDATE on status=running stops the summary email being sent twice
The failure count excludes fan-out job failures and also covers timeouts through failed()
Modern attributes throughout: #[Tries], #[Timeout], #[Fillable], #[Scope]. The mailable attaches with fromStorageDisk and an explicit mime type
Verified end to end with a real array mailer: attachments are built and emails are sent
Tests cover the failing account, storage failure means no email, the empty run, queue placement and the inactive filter

No pruning is scheduled for job_batches or failed_jobs, so the queue tables grow forever

app/Jobs/FinalizeStatementRun.php:19-29 checks status, then updates. That is not atomic, so two concurrent finally invocations could both send the summary
antipatterns: app/Jobs/FinalizeStatementRun.php:11 sits in App\Jobs but is not a job; it is a plain batch callback object
app/Jobs/QueueStatementJobs.php:12 has no Tries limit or cancelled() check. Its retry count is left to worker defaults, and a retry duplicates the fan-out
tests/Feature/StatementRunTest.php:17-22 drainQueue runs queue:work twice with time travel, which makes the suite slow (about 24s)
strengths: Retries with backoff, plus an idempotent file check (exists before put), so a retry does not regenerate the PDF
Uses the batch's failedJobs as the source of truth for the failure count
Tests run a real database queue with workers, which is realistic, and include an idempotency test
Blade views for the mail bodies; clean and minimal code

bugs: No pruning is scheduled for job_batches or failed_jobs (routes/console.php unchanged), so the queue tables grow forever
failed_accounts = $batch->failedJobs would count a failure of the fan-out job as an account failure (edge case)
total_accounts is snapshotted in the request while the fan-out re-queries later, so the counts can drift
antipatterns: app/Actions/StartStatementRun.php:21-25 special-cases zero accounts and finalizes synchronously in the request. The batch already handles an empty fan-out, so this is an extra branch
app/Mail/StatementReady.php:16 takes a StatementRun $run that the mailable never uses
The finally closure is serialized with SerializableClosure. That works, but an invokable class would be more refactor-safe
strengths: SendStatement uses #[Tries(3), Backoff([30,120]), Timeout(120), DeleteWhenMissingModels] together with an idempotent exists-then-put, so transient errors are retried without regenerating the PDF and the email goes out only after the file exists
The fan-out job is #[Tries(1)], which avoids duplicate fan-out on retry; lazyById chunked batch->add runs on the dedicated queue
FinalizeStatementRun claims the run atomically with a conditional UPDATE before emailing finance, so the summary is sent at most once
Verified end to end with a real array mailer: the PDF attachment is built and emails are sent
The failure-path test drives real queue workers through retries and backoff with time travel; it uses the Pest expect chain on properties

v.rationale: All three use the same design: a batch that holds a single fan-out job, which uses lazyById to add chunked per-account jobs on a 'statements' queue, plus allowFailures and finally. None schedule queue:prune-batches or failed-job pruning, so all three miss the requirement that queue tables do not grow forever. impl-2 imports a non-existent class (Illuminate\Mail\Attachments\Attachment). Its tests pass because Mail::fake never builds the attachments, but my probe with a real array mailer showed every account failing, so in production it would send no statements at all. It ranks last. impl-3 and impl-1 both work end to end. impl-3 is better for resilience: retries with backoff, idempotent PDF storage, and a fan-out job set to a single try so a retry cannot queue every account twice. impl-1 catches every Throwable with Tries(1), so transient errors are never retried. Its fan-out job has Tries(3), so a retry would queue every account a second time. impl-1's own failure counting is slightly more accurate, because a fan-out failure is not counted as an account failure, but its weaker retry semantics put it second.
